title: Keep a local variable
summary: A T-SQL variable starts with @. DECLARE gives it a type and an optional starting value.
introduction: A T-SQL variable starts with @. DECLARE gives it a type and an optional starting value. Your task: Change the variable to another sample name.
learningObjectives: Change the variable to another sample name.
Explain the example for keep a local variable

blocks.text: A T-SQL variable starts with @. DECLARE gives it a type and an optional starting value.
Use SQL Server 2019+ in a separate practice database with a SQL editor. T-SQL is different from the SQLite engine on this site, so these examples are for that separate tool.

blocks.code:
DECLARE @name nvarchar(40)=N'Mia';
SELECT N'Hello, '+@name AS greeting;
blocks.title: Keep a local variable

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The result is Hello, Mia. N marks a Unicode string literal.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Choose a text length that fits the intended value. A variable exists only in its batch or procedure scope.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change the variable to another sample name.
